original.target_description: Experiments 1a–1c pooled across languages: vowel sound × product category interaction in the 2 × 2 × 4 mixed ANOVA, section 3.2.1, printed F(1, 367)=63.87. This is the pooled interaction, not a language-specific interaction.

n.sample_role: Participants across the three separate experimental samples, pooled for the critical mixed ANOVA; vowel sound within participants, product category and experiment between participants.
n.exclusions: No participant exclusions reported in the supplied methods/results. Gender missingness (one in 1a and one in 1b) is included in the printed sample counts, not a participant exclusion. Translation errors reduce word pairs in Chinese logographic conditions, not the stated participant sample.
n.location: p. 276, §3.1.1 Participants, procedure, and measures; p. 277, §3.2.1 Effects of sound as a function of product

notes: Identity verified within supplied canonical text: title Sound symbolism effects across languages: Implications for global brand names; authors L. J. Shrum, T. M. Lowrey, David Luna, D. B. Lerman, Min Liu; DOI 10.1016/j.ijresmar.2012.03.002; International Journal of Research in Marketing 29 (2012), 275–279. Five-page primary research report with methods, results, tables and references; not an abstract-only excerpt or secondary article. No PDF was supplied. Only assigned n_o reviewed; other statistic fields and replication are unassigned placeholders. 106 (Experiment 1a, French sample) + 88 (Experiment 1b, Spanish sample) + 181 (Experiment 1c, Chinese sample) = 375 participants. Separate experiments/country samples are mutually exclusive; the critical analysis explicitly combines all three. Alphabetic/logographic conditions are subdivisions of 1c, not additional samples. N is not inferred from degrees of freedom.
